e52255.title: Windows 11 (build 26200) + AMD RX 9070: Chromium GPU process fails during startup (`GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`)
e52255.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

Electron 39.8.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should launch normally.


Maybe duplicate of : `electron/electron#52098`
`electron/electron#51761`

Affected applications:

* Obsidian 1.12.7
* Signal Desktop 8.17.0
* Discord (latest)

Not affected:

* Visual Studio Code 1.126.0

## Environment

* OS: Windows 11 Pro
* Build: 26200.8737
* GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070
* Driver: 32.0.31021.5001
* Secondary GPU: AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics






### Actual Behavior

## Actual Behavior

Multiple Electron applications terminate during startup.

The logs consistently end with:

```text
[FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415]
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

Signal additionally reports repeated GPU process failures before aborting:

```text
GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
```

Windows Event Viewer records Application Error (Event ID 1000) with exception code:

```
0x80000003
```

The faulting module is the application executable itself (e.g. `Obsidian.exe`, `Signal.exe`).

## Reproduction

Launching Obsidian normally:

```powershell
& "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\Obsidian\Obsidian.exe"
```

Results in:

* application exits almost immediately
* log ends with `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.`

The same behavior is observed with Signal Desktop and Discord.

## Startup Flag Testing

### `--in-process-gpu`

Launching with:

```text
--in-process-gpu
```

changes the behavior:

* the process no longer exits immediately
* however, the application window is not rendered correctly (GUI is missing / blank)

### Four-flag combination

Launching with:

```text
--disable-gpu
--disable-gpu-compositing
--disable-software-rasterizer
--in-process-gpu
```

changes the behavior further.

In Safe Mode, this combination allows the UI to render instead of immediately terminating.

Outside Safe Mode, startup behavior changes, but rendering is still incomplete or absent.

The fact that `--in-process-gpu` consistently changes the failure mode suggests the issue is related to Chromium's GPU process initialization.

## Diagnostics Already Performed

* Updated AMD driver to latest available version
* `sfc /scannow`
* Windows Defender scan
* Malwarebytes scan
* HDR disabled
* Safe Mode testing
* AMD Radeon Software terminated
* DxDiag reports no display or DirectX problems

None of the above resolved the issue.

If there are additional Chromium or Electron logging flags that would help diagnose why the GPU process exits, I would be happy to collect and provide them.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Visual Studio Code launches normally on the same machine.

This suggests the issue is not a complete Electron failure, but may depend on the Electron/Chromium version or GPU initialization path used by different applications.

e52263.title: Allow monospaced digit fonts for menu item labels on macOS
e52263.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description On macOS, menu item labels are rendered with the system menu font, whose digits are proportional. So any menu showing a column of numbers comes out jagged, because e.g. `11:15` renders narrower than `09:45`: There's currently no way around this: `MenuItem.label` maps to `NSMenuItem.title`, and Electron exposes neither `attributedTitle` nor any font option. In a native app this is a one-liner: set `attributedTitle` with `monospacedDigitSystemFontOfSize:`, the SF variant with tabular figures that's otherwise identical to the menu font. #22363 solved the same problem for the tray title with `tray.setTitle(title, { fontType: 'monospacedDigit' })`. Menu item labels never got the equivalent, so a tray calendar can align its countdown but not the time column in its dropdown. ### Proposed Solution The same `fontType` option on `MenuItem`, macOS-only like `toolTip`: ```js new MenuItem({ label: "11:15 Doctor's appointment", fontType: 'monospacedDigit' }) ``` The implementation looks small: when the option is set, `electron_menu_controller.mm` renders the label via `attributedTitle` with the corresponding font variant, analogous to the `fontType` handling in `tray_icon_cocoa.mm`. Supporting both tray values (`monospaced` and `monospacedDigit`) keeps the two APIs symmetric. ### Alternatives Considered - Padding with figure spaces (U+2007): Still unequal widths, the digits themselves are proportional - Unicode fullwidth/monospace digits: Wrong font, looks out of place - Pre-rendering the time column into template `NativeImage` icons: What we ship today – works well, but adds a lot of machinery for one line of AppKit ### Additional Information I attached [menu-item-font-type.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29671470/menu-item-font-type.patch) mirroring the `toolTip` per-item plumbing and the tray `fontType` implementation. It was drafted with Claude Fable 5, and I'm currently unable to build Electron locally – so it's untested. Happy to open a PR from it so CI can validate it, or for a maintainer to adopt or rework it instead.

e52383.title: [Bug]: navigator.usb.requestDevice() crashes the browser process (SIGSEGV) on a named session partition
e52383.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.1.1

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 (25F84)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — every version I tested reproduces (41.10.0, 41.10.2, 43.1.1); not bisected further back.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Calling `navigator.usb.requestDevice({ filters: [] })` from a window whose `webPreferences.partition` is a **named session** should reject with `NotFoundError` — exactly as it does with the default session — when no device is selected / no `select-usb-device` handler is registered.

### Actual Behavior

The **browser process** crashes with `SIGSEGV` (`EXC_BAD_ACCESS` on `CrBrowserMain`).

The trigger is the named session partition: with the **default** session the identical call rejects cleanly with `NotFoundError: No device selected`. `navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice()` crashes the same way. Registering a `select-usb-device` handler that cancels the request (`event.preventDefault(); callback()`) does **not** prevent the crash — the fault happens in native code before the JS handler resolves.

```
Exception Type:    EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000100
Triggered by Thread: 0  CrBrowserMain

Thread 0 Crashed:: CrBrowserMain
0  Electron Framework  v8::CppHeap::Create(...)
1  Electron Framework  node::PrincipalRealm::...
```

(Symbol names are nearest-export approximations from a release build; the fault is inside V8 / cppgc internals during device-chooser setup.)

Regarding the Chromium question above: the trigger is an Electron-specific `webPreferences.partition` (named session), which has no web-page-settable equivalent in stock Chrome, so I can't reproduce it directly there. The crash itself is in the Chromium-layer device-chooser path, so a Chromium root cause is still possible.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/boutetnico/cd2005b668f680b47abab2056b3fccc6

### Additional Information

The only difference between the crashing and non-crashing runs is a single `webPreferences.partition` value. In the gist, `main.js` calls `requestDevice()` from the main process via `webContents.executeJavaScript(code, /* userGesture */ true)` on `did-finish-load`; flipping the `USE_DEFAULT_SESSION` constant to `true` gives the non-crashing control case. No device or hardware is required — the crash happens while opening the device chooser.

Reproduced identically on:

| Electron | Chromium | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 41.10.0 | 146 | SIGSEGV |
| 41.10.2 | 146 | SIGSEGV |
| 43.1.1 | 150 | SIGSEGV |

e52643.body:

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.

### Electron Version

30.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

win 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should not allow Windows system DLLs or optional DLLs to be loaded from the application installation directory unless explicitly intended. DLL loading should use secure Windows DLL loading mechanisms and trusted system locations to prevent DLL side-loading.

### Actual Behavior

The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Summary:**
- We observed behavior that may indicate a DLL side-loading vulnerability in Electron 30 on Windows.

**Environment**
- Electron: 30.0.0
- Platform: Windows 11 (64-bit)
- Packaging: Electron Forge (MSI)

**Steps to Reproduce**
- Build and install an Electron application.
- Monitor the application startup using Process Monitor.
- Observe that Windows probes the application installation directory for optional system DLLs, including:
   - CRYPTSP.dll
   - dbghelp.dll
   - version.dll
   - winhttp.dll
   - userenv.dll
   - dbgcore.dll

- Create a custom DLL (proof of concept) with a payload  (for example, launching Calculator).
- Rename the DLL to match one of the DLL names observed during startup (for example, CRYPTSP.dll).
- Copy the DLL into the application's installation directory.
- Launch the application.

**Observed Behavior**
- The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

e52738.title: macOS: audio: 'loopbackWithMute' in setDisplayMediaRequestHandler never captures data with useSystemPicker: false
e52738.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.3.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS Tahoe 26.5.2 (arm64 / Apple Silicon) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — have not found a version where this works via a custom picker. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When `session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` is used with `useSystemPicker: false` (i.e. the app supplies its own picker UI and resolves the callback with a `desktopCapturer` source plus `audio: 'loopback'` or `audio: 'loopbackWithMute'`), the resulting audio `MediaStreamTrack` should actually capture system audio, the same way it does when `useSystemPicker: true` is used instead. ### Actual Behavior The audio track is created (`kind: "audio"`, `label: "System audio"`), so the API call itself succeeds, but the track's `readyState` is `"ended"` from the very first observation, and no audio data is ever captured — an `AnalyserNode` attached to the track reports `peakAmplitude: 0` at every sample, forever. The video track from the same `getDisplayMedia()` call works fine (`readyState: "live"`, frames render normally) — only the audio side fails. Swapping the same request handler to `useSystemPicker: true` (letting Electron/macOS own the whole picker UI) makes system-audio capture work correctly and also correctly triggers the macOS "would like to record system audio" TCC permission prompt. With `useSystemPicker: false`, that TCC prompt never appears at all — which is consistent with the underlying native audio-capture session never actually starting, even though the JS-level API returns a track as if it had. This makes `audio: 'loopback'`/`'loopbackWithMute'` unusable for any app that wants to keep its own custom screen-share picker UI while also offering a "share system audio" option — the only way to get working system audio is to hand the entire picker over to `useSystemPicker: true`, which replaces the app's own UI. Reproduces identically on an ad-hoc `electron .` run and on a `Developer ID`-signed, hardened-runtime, notarization-skipped, `/Applications`-installed packaged build — so this isn't a code-signing or Gatekeeper/TCC-staleness issue. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/anildigital/9a195654a687524fb544db62894466fe ### Additional Information Steps to reproduce with the gist: 1. `npm install` in the gist's directory, then `npm start` (or `electron .`). 2. The renderer calls `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true })`. 3. Watch the on-screen log: the audio track appears with `readyState=ended` immediately, and the peak-amplitude readout stays at `0.0000` indefinitely, while the video track stays `live`. 4. For comparison, change `useSystemPicker: false` to `useSystemPicker: true` in `main.js` and repeat — the native macOS picker appears, the TCC "record your system audio" prompt fires, and after granting it, real audio is captured (non-zero peak amplitude).
In-depth investigation

We believe the root cause is that macOS's system-audio capture (the ScreenCaptureKit-backed Core Audio Tap, gated behind the separate "System Audio Recording Only" TCC permission introduced in newer macOS versions) is only ever started by Electron when Electron's own native picker (`useSystemPicker: true`) drives the capture end-to-end. When an app supplies its own `desktopCapturer`-selected source through a custom picker instead, the `'loopback'`/`'loopbackWithMute'` audio request appears to be accepted and a track handle is handed back, but the corresponding native capture session is never actually wired up — no TCC prompt is ever shown for the app through this path, and `getUserMedia`/`getDisplayMedia` never delivers audio samples. We were unable to find any workaround from the app side (no combination of Chromium command-line switches changed the result), and confirmed the failure is independent of code signing, notarization, and running from `/Applications` vs. an ad-hoc build directory.

### Problem Description

Hi,

On Wayland, CJK input methods currently only get a cursor rectangle from the app. Because the cursor moves while typing Pinyin, the candidate popup jumps around constantly.

The proposed fix in wayland-protocols is to let apps also send a preedit rectangle, so the input method can anchor the popup to the start of the preedit instead of the moving cursor. See the discussion here:
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/517
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/521

Since Electron apps like VS Code and Slack are very popular on Linux, it would make a huge difference if Electron could send the preedit rectangle via zwp_text_input_v3 (in addition to the cursor rectangle). Without that, input methods can't fix the jumping even if they support the new protocol.

Is there any plan to implement this? I'd be glad to test an early build.

Thanks!

input methods

input methods

e53213.title: Tray icon missing on GNOME (Wayland) in 44.0.0 / 43.4.1+: StatusNotifierItem registration is rejected
e53213.body:
### Electron Version

44.0.0 (also 44.0.0-beta.6, 43.4.1, 43.4.2)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME with the default ubuntu-appindicators extension, Wayland and Xorg sessions

### What arch are you using?

x64, arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

44.0.0-beta.5 / 43.4.0 (icon registers; see #52674 for the separate menu problem those had), 42.x fully working

### Expected Behavior

`new Tray(image)` registers a StatusNotifierItem with `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` and the icon shows in the GNOME top bar.

### Actual Behavior

Nothing is registered with the watcher (`busctl --user get-property org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher /StatusNotifierWatcher org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` never lists the app). On Wayland there is no tray icon at all; on Xorg the legacy XEmbed fallback icon appears instead.

The item calls `RegisterStatusNotifierItem("org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1")`, i.e. the well-known name with the object path appended. GNOME's watcher treats an argument that does not start with `/` as a bus name, `GetNameOwner` fails on that string, and the registration is refused, after which the SNI implementation is torn down. This came in with the cherry-pick of https://crrev.com/c/8250459 in #52951 (44-x-y) and #52952 (43-x-y); upstream fixed it a week later in https://crrev.com/c/8272040 (in Chromium 154.0.8016.0, so `main` already has it), which registers the plain well-known name and exports the item at `/StatusNotifierItem` again.

### Testcase Gist URL

```js
const { app, Tray, Menu, nativeImage } = require('electron');
app.on('ready', () => {
  const t = new Tray(nativeImage.createFromPath('icon.png'));
  t.setContextMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate([{ label: 'Quit', role: 'quit' }]));
});
```

Per-version result against a watcher that resolves items the way the GNOME extension does:

| version | RegisterStatusNotifierItem argument | result |
|---|---|---|
| 42.10.0 | `:1.1` | ok |
| 43.4.0, 44.0.0-beta.5 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` | registered (menu issue is #52674) |
| 43.4.1, 44.0.0-beta.6, 44.0.0 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1` | `NameHasNoOwner`, registration refused |

e53376.title: [Bug]: webContents.debugger use-after-free: cppgc-managed Debugger never detaches its DevToolsAgentHostClient, crashing the browser process
e53376.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.5.0 (also reproduced on 43.4.1)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6.2

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — the affected code path was introduced with the cppgc/Oilpan migration of `electron::api::Debugger`

### Expected Behavior

Attaching `webContents.debugger` to a WebContents (in our case, `<webview>` guest contents), receiving CDP notifications, and later letting the WebContents be destroyed should never crash the browser process, regardless of GC timing.

### Actual Behavior

The browser process segfaults (`EXC_BAD_ACCESS / KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS` at `0x10`/`0x18` — a null/dangling pointer plus member offset) on `CrBrowserMain`. We collected three crashes in one day across two Electron versions (41.5.0 and 43.4.1), in two distinct but related signatures.

**Signature A (2 of 3 crashes) — inbound CDP notification dispatched to a freed client** (symbolicated from macOS `.ips` via breakpad symbols, Electron 41.5.0):

```
0  content::DevToolsSession::DispatchProtocolNotification(...)
1  blink::mojom::DevToolsSessionHostStubDispatch::Accept(...)
2  mojo::InterfaceEndpointClient::HandleIncomingMessageThunk::Accept(mojo::Message*)
3  mojo::MessageDispatcher::Accept(mojo::Message*)
4  mojo::InterfaceEndpointClient::HandleIncomingMessage(mojo::Message*)
5  IPC::ChannelAssociatedGroupController::AcceptOnEndpointThread(...)
6  base::TaskAnnotator::RunTaskImpl(base::PendingTask&)
7  base::sequence_manager::internal::ThreadControllerWithMessagePumpImpl::DoWork()
8  base::MessagePumpCFRunLoopBase::RunWorkSource(void*)
   ... CFRunLoop / NSApplication run loop ...
```

On 43.4.1 the same crash appears with frame 0 in `content::DevToolsSession::DispatchProtocolResponseOrNotification(content::DevToolsAgentHostClient*, ...)`.

**Signature B (1 of 3) — WebContents teardown force-detaches sessions into a freed client** (Electron 41.5.0):

```
0  content::DevToolsAgentHostImpl::ForceDetachAllSessionsImpl()
1  content::RenderFrameDevToolsAgentHost::DestroyOnRenderFrameGone()
2  content::RenderFrameDevToolsAgentHost::FrameDeleted(...)
3  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsObserverList::NotifyObservers(...)
4  content::WebContentsImpl::OnFrameTreeNodeDestroyed(content::FrameTreeNode*)
5  content::FrameTree::Shutdown()
6  content::WebContentsImpl::~WebContentsImpl()
7  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsTreeNode::DestroyOwnedInnerWebContents(...)
8  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsTreeNode::DetachInnerWebContents(...)
9  content::WebContentsImpl::WebContentsTreeNode::OnFrameTreeNodeDestroyed(...)
10 content::FrameTreeNode::~FrameTreeNode()
11 content::RenderFrameHostImpl::ResetChildren()
12 content::FrameTree::Shutdown()
13 content::WebContentsImpl::~WebContentsImpl()
14 electron::InspectableWebContents::~InspectableWebContents()
15 electron::api::WebContents::~WebContents()
16 electron::api::WebContents::DeleteThisIfAlive()
17 base::TaskAnnotator::RunTaskImpl(base::PendingTask&)
   ... message pump ...
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Root-cause analysis** (from reading the v41.5.0 / main sources; we do not have a minimal repro yet — the crash depends on GC timing, which matches its "random, tens of minutes apart" occurrence in production):

`electron::api::Debugger` is now a cppgc/Oilpan-managed `gin::Wrappable`, but it registers itself with content as a **raw** `content::DevToolsAgentHostClient*` via `agent_host_->AttachClient(this)`:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L119

Its destructor never detaches that client:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L35

```cc
Debugger::~Debugger() = default;
```

`DetachClient` is only called from the explicit JS-facing `Debugger::Detach()`:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L126-L131

The only strong root keeping an attached `Debugger` alive is the owning `api::WebContents`'s member:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v41.5.0/shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.h#L783

```cc
cppgc::Persistent<api::Debugger> debugger_;
```

So once the `api::WebContents` wrapper goes away (e.g. `<webview>` guest destruction via the posted `DeleteThisIfAlive()` task, as in Signature B), nothing on the content side owns or pins the still-attached client. When cppgc sweeps the `Debugger` while `DevToolsSession`/`DevToolsAgentHost` still hold the raw client pointer:

- the next CDP notification from the renderer dispatches into freed memory (**Signature A** — easy to hit with chatty domains like `Network.enable` / `Log.enable` / `Page.startScreencast`), or
- a later WebContents-tree teardown reaches `ForceDetachAllSessionsImpl()`, which invokes `client->AgentHostClosed()` on freed memory (**Signature B**). Sweep order between the `api::WebContents` and its `Debugger` in the same GC cycle is unspecified, so the Debugger can be gone by the time the WebContents teardown runs.

The bug is still present on `main` — `Debugger::~Debugger() = default;`:
https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/shell/browser/api/electron_api_debugger.cc#L36

Before the cppgc migration this was masked because the wrappable's deterministic destruction paths differed; with Oilpan, destruction is decoupled from the last use, so the raw client pointer in content outlives the object.

**Suggested fix**: ensure the client is detached before the object can be reclaimed — e.g. call `agent_host_->DetachClient(this)` in `~Debugger()` (mirroring `Detach()`), and/or detach in a `WebContentsDestroyed()` observer hook so the session never survives its client.

**Context in which we hit this**: our app attaches `webContents.debugger.attach("1.3")` to `<webview>` guest WebContents and enables `Runtime`/`Network`/`Log`/`Accessibility` (constant notification stream). Guests are routinely destroyed and recreated. Crashes appear minutes to tens of minutes later, aligned with GC pressure rather than any user action. Happy to provide the full `.ips` reports or symbolicated dumps on request.

e53610.body:

### Electron Version

Shipped with Signal Desktop 8.26.0 (Electron 32.x range)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Shipped with Signal Desktop 8.26.0 (Electron 32.x range)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Signal Desktop (and other Electron apps) should start normally with a visible window and working renderer.

### Actual Behavior

Signal silently crashes at startup with no window shown. The GPU subprocess exits with `STATUS_BREAKPOINT` (`0x80000003` / exit code `-2147483645`). This is a related but distinct variant from the original reports in #32440 which showed `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (`0xC0000005`).

Windows Application Event Log (Event ID 1000):
```text
Faulting application: Signal.exe
Exception code: 0x80000003 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT)
Fault offset: 0x0000000006fefb69  ← identical across every crash attempt
```

Running with `--disable-gpu` surfaces the GPU subprocess crash explicitly:
```text
[ERROR:gpu_process_host.cc:1108] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[FATAL:gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:416] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

**Secondary issue:** Even after working around the startup crash with `--in-process-gpu`, newly spawned renderer processes (e.g. Help → About window) crash with the same exit code:
```text
Render process is gone
Error: Reason: crashed, Exit Code: -2147483645
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Hardware
- GPU: Intel® Iris® Xe Graphics — Tiger Lake (`PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_9A49`, HP subsystem `87FE103C`)
- Drivers tested: `31.0.101.5186` (Jan 2024) and `32.0.101.7088` (Jun 2026) — both affected

### Diagnostics Ruled Out
- Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS): not enabled
- Hardware Shadow Stack / CET (`UserShadowStack`): NOTSET  
- No third-party AV or EDR (Windows Defender only)
- Fault offset `0x06fefb69` is deterministic across all crash attempts

### Workaround
`--in-process-gpu` flag allows the app to start. `--disable-gpu` alone does **not** fix it (GPU subprocess still crashes).

### Related Issues
- `electron/electron#32440` (closed — original report, different exit code `0xC0000005`)
- `signalapp/Signal-Desktop#5721` (open — Intel integrated graphics requiring GPU flags)
- `signalapp/Signal-Desktop#7828` (open — renderer crash on Windows 11)

e53747.title: Use WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP to reduce memory usage when creating Windows in Microsoft Windows
e53747.body:

### Problem Description

The Windows windowing system was built with GDI, so it creates a default GDI canvas for every window. This canvas uses 3 bytes per pixel, about 6 MB for a 1080p screen. For self-rendering apps like Electron, this canvas is unnecessary. Since the memory is not allocated by the application itself but by the DWM, there is no simple way to accurately measure and test it. The only way to disable it is to pass WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP to CreateWindowEx. Electron Apps should use this optimization.

Background:
`microsoft/terminal#20655`
`microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#11523`

### Proposed Solution

Update the document native-code-and-electron-cpp-win32.md

none

e54035.title: Variable refresh rate (VRR) performance issue under Gnome 50 (Wayland)
e54035.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.10.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 26.04 (Wayland)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Apologies in advance for the peculiar bug-report, but this truly appears to be an Electron related issue...

Setup is as follows: Laptop with an internal 2.8k-screen, variable refresh rate (VRR) enabled; an external 4k-monitor (its VRR state seems irrelevant). Both screens are in-use.

Run two Electron-based apps; one on either monitor; both of their windows maximised (not full-screen).

I would expect the (drawing) performance of both applications to be identical, and to be good/"smooth".

### Actual Behavior

It is not.

Performance of the maximised window on the laptop's screen is terrible (feels like "15 FPS"). The moment the Electron app on the other/external monitor goes from maximised the windowed, performance of the maximised window on the laptop screen returns to normal.

In other words: Performance is as expected in all situations, _except_ when two Electron-based apps run with maximised windows on the two separate monitors (where one has VRR enabled; the VRR state of the other screen seems not to matter).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This screen capture illustrates the problem perhaps better than the above description:
- https://drive.proton.me/urls/HTKT29NV30#2mE6vTjCMBDe – 5k h264 (Firefox doesn't seem to want to play it; Chromium has no problems)

The effect is diminished in the capture as a result of the load put on the system by capturing. The difference in v-sync performance is still pretty obvious though. The external monitor is on the top left, the laptop's screen on the bottom right.

Identical behaviour is observed with other (recent) Electron apps (Joplin, Electron 42; Slack, Electron 44). VS Code offers the easiest reproduction as one can simply run [vsynctester.com](https://www.vsynctester.com/) in its internal browser. Any combination of VS Code, Joplin, and Slack (so I would assume "any" Electron-based app) can be used to reproduce the issue.

The problem does not occur with Chromium itself (tested with ungoogled-chromium `152.0.7977.82`), nor with other applications (i.e., Firefox works fine too).

Disabling VRR on the laptop's screen resolves the issue.

The converse setup (laptop screen with VRR disabled; 4k-monitor with VRR enabled) doesn't exhibit the issue either. Perhaps a result of the difference in VRR ranges?

- 4k-monitor: 48-120 Hz

e54317.title: WebAuthn request that needs a security-key PIN crashes the browser process on Linux
e54317.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.4.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS (Arch-based), Linux 7.1.8-1-cachyos, KDE Plasma 6 (Wayland) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version None found. 43.4.1, 42.9.0, and 39.8.10 also crashed with SIGTRAP, but those runs followed an earlier crash that had left the YubiKey 5 unresponsive, so they are consistent with the finding rather than clean data. The clean single-key runs below are on 43.4.0. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When a WebAuthn request reaches a USB security key that requires a PIN and Electron has no PIN prompt to show, the request should reject (for example with `NotAllowedError`) and the app should keep running. ### Actual Behavior The browser process dies with SIGTRAP from a CHECK about 0.7 s after launch, during `navigator.credentials.create()` and before the key is touched. With `--enable-logging=stderr --vmodule=device_event_log_impl=1`, the FIDO log ends right after Chromium reads the key's PIN retry count: ``` FIDO: DEBUG: fido_device.cc:70 The device supports the CTAP2 protocol. FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:91 <- 0x6 (kAuthenticatorClientPin) {1: 2, 2: 7} FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:188 -> {5: 0} FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:91 <- 0x6 (kAuthenticatorClientPin) {1: 2, 2: 1} FIDO: DEBUG: ctap2_device_operation.h:188 -> {3: 8} ``` `{5: 0}` answers the UV-retries query and `{3: 8}` reports 8 PIN retries. Results with the gist on 43.4.0: | Keys plugged in | Result | |---|---| | YubiKey 5 only | Crash during `create()`, no touch | | YubiKey 4 only | `create()` OK, `get()` OK | | Both; YubiKey 4 touched | `create()` OK, `get()` OK; the log shows a clean cancel of the YubiKey 5's operation | The YubiKey 5 (USB `1050:0406`, firmware 5.8.0) reports `alwaysUv: true`, `uv: true`, `clientPin: true`, `bioEnroll: true`, `makeCredUvNotRqd: false`, and `pinUvAuthToken: true`, so every operation needs user verification. The YubiKey 4 (USB `1050:0407`) is U2F only. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/nisavid/a7e5438b6ceef5a0761898dc99ec6b64 ### Additional Information The gist is a minimal main-process app that serves `index.html` on `http://localhost` and runs `navigator.credentials.create()` for a non-resident credential with `userVerification: "discouraged"`, then `navigator.credentials.get()` with that credential. `get()` takes `userVerification` from the `uv` query parameter (default `discouraged`); `REPRO_QUERY='?uv=preferred'` sets it, which the crashing runs used, though the single-key run crashed inside `create()` before `get()` ran. Run it with a PIN-protected FIDO2 key plugged in: ``` electron . --enable-logging=stderr --vmodule=device_event_log_impl=1 ``` This is narrower than #24573, which tracks the missing Linux FIDO2 PIN UI: here a request that needs the PIN takes the browser process down instead of rejecting. It surfaced in the Proton Pass desktop app (`/usr/lib/electron43/electron /usr/share/proton-pass/app.asar`), whose in-app sign-in crashed three times on 2026-09-24 with a main-thread stack identical to the gist's. Chrome was not tested.
In-depth investigation

The distro `electron43` binary is stripped. `systemd-coredump` labels frame 0 `cppgc::internal::FatalImpl`, but that 7-byte exported symbol (`push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; int3; ud2`) is an identical-code-folded `IMMEDIATE_CRASH` stub, so the name is a misattribution. Identifying the other frames by the source-path strings their functions reference gives: a `device.mojom.HidConnection` read, then `device/fido/hid/fido_hid_device.cc` (message received), then the `device/fido/ctap2_device_operation.h` response callback, then the crash stub. The gist's core has the same stack hash as the Proton Pass cores. My reading, as inference: the key's `alwaysUv` makes the request need PIN/UV, the request handler moves on to PIN collection after reading the retry counts, and with no PIN UI on Linux the browser process hits a CHECK instead of failing the request.
